purpose: Exemplar of a well-formed run over multiple docs with a categorical topic filter. Use this to eyeball what 'good' looks like when eval scores dip.

input.question: Which customers raised pricing concerns in the last 12 months?

expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_1_filter: Scope should include EVERY doc whose topics_tagged contains 'pricing' AND whose date is within the last 12 months of today. Content-shaped filters are inclusive when unsure (rule 3).
expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_2_rescope: Should collapse to something like: 'Did the customer raise pricing concerns in this meeting?' — no compound clauses, no time filter (that was applied in step 1).
expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_4_signals: Each in-scope doc's sub-agent emits a signal only if the body affirmatively surfaces a pricing concern. Docs with no pricing content emit no_signal — NOT a signal with 'raised_pricing_concern: false'.
expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_7_aggregate: Answer text must cite each customer with an inline [sN] marker. Never invents a customer that isn't in the signals.

exemplar_signals.finding_summary: Fintrust's VP of Customer Operations pushed back on Voxly's per-minute pricing as too steep for their expected call volume.
exemplar_signals.reference_text_shape: A verbatim quote from the transcript body where the Fintrust rep says something like 'thirty-two cents a minute is a lot for us — the volume adds up quickly'.

exemplar_signals.finding_summary: Nimbus Health's CFO framed the annual contract value gap ($490K paid, half unused) as a P&L drag driving churn risk.
exemplar_signals.reference_text_shape: A verbatim quote where the Nimbus CFO cites the specific dollar figure and links it to their P&L or ROI conversation.

exemplar_response_text:
Four customers surfaced pricing concerns in the last 12 months:

- **Fintrust** [s1] pushed back on Voxly's per-minute rate during their August discovery call.
- **Nimbus Health** [s2] framed a $490K unused-contract-value gap as churn-driving pressure on their P&L in May 2026.
- **Anchorline Logistics** [s3] and **Globex** [s4] raised pricing during their respective calls (see cited quotes).

Acme Corp and Beacon SaaS were NOT among the customers who raised pricing concerns during this window.
anti_patterns_this_run_should_avoid: Emitting a signal with `raised_pricing_concern: false` for docs with no pricing content — use no_signal instead.
Restating the reference_text verbatim in the response_text — the UI shows it separately.
Citing customer names not in the metadata of the in-scope docs.
Missing the [sN] markers on any factual claim in the aggregated answer.
Fabricating dollar figures or dates not present in either the metadata or the reference_text.
